question.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\operatorname{cot}⁡(2t),$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+1)=-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(-\operatorname{cot}⁡(2t))}{-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\frac{(2{csc}^{2}⁡(2t))}{-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{csc}^{3}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=\frac{\pi }{4},$ and we get

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,{|}_{t\,=\,\frac{\pi }{4}}=-\frac{1}{4}{csc}^{3}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{1}{4}.
$$
